title: Omphalos
html_source:
Greek for “navel,” as in the center of the world. Refers to Stephen’s dream of making Ireland a center of high culture. However, they are currently in a Martello tower, a British military institution, a reflection of Stephen’s unease with Haines.

Also in the The Odyssey one of Homer’s epithets for Ogygia, Calypso’s islands “navel of the sea.”
